title: The Woman Who Refused to Be Interrupted

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager keeps being talked over at the gathering: others insist she finish, or she leaves and says it elsewhere.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has tried three times at the gathering to explain her plan for the fish drying racks, and three times someone has talked over her. (friend) has noticed. So have several others. What should happen?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) stands up and says, loudly, that (subject) has not finished. The next person who interrupts gets glared at by half the gathering. (subject) finishes. Her plan is good. It is adopted. She thanks (friend) afterwards, and says next time she will not wait for help.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) walks out and builds a drying rack her own way by the beach. It works better than any other. Within a month, everyone is copying it. Nobody interrupts her at the next gathering.
